raw_response.rationale: The paper conducts inferential county-level spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I) and OLS linear regressions (N = 3,143 U.S. counties using 2008-2013 ACS and 2013 USDA ERS Urban Influence Codes) on a valid Criterion 4 outcome (percentage of occupied housing units lacking complete plumbing facilities). However, all empirically tested independent variables in the regressions (Table 3, PDF p. 9) are purely demographic, socioeconomic, rurality, and geographic division predictors (racial/ethnic population shares, median household income, unemployment, gender, median age, high school graduation rate, USDA 1-9 urbanicity code, and Census division dummies). No rule-type legal, administrative, municipal-incorporation, reservation-jurisdiction, tenure, zoning, tariff, governance, or ownership exposure (narrow Criterion 2) is quantitatively measured or tested; legal/institutional mechanisms such as California municipal incorporation exclusion, reservation governance, utility zoning ('blue lining'), and Detroit water shutoffs are discussed only qualitatively/anecdotally as motivating context and data limitations (PDF pp. 13-14, 17). Thus, the inferential estimates do not belong to any SWiM legal/institutional family.
